title: Traffic gating and rollback orchestrator for staged model rollouts
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: We need a single expressive engine that composes traffic-gating policies, stepwise schedules, and rollback rules for staged model rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow). Existing configs are fragmented across the Console, runtime, and infra policies which causes safety gaps and operator confusion.

Goal: Implement a policy composer and orchestration layer that: (1) expresses traffic splits and multi-step schedules; (2) evaluates multi-metric guardrails (latency, error-rate, quality delta, cost) in realtime; (3) supports shadow traffic and A/B measurement windows; (4) performs automated safe rollback or hold actions; (5) surfaces explainable reasons and an audit trail in the Console.

Success signals: customers can define a rollout in one config, preview the expected step schedule, run a dry-run simulation, see metric gating reasoning in the Console, and safely enable auto-rollback with well-scoped SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout config schema v1 accepted by Console and runtime APIs
Simulator can execute a 6-step progressive ramp and produce estimated traffic/time charts
Guardrail evaluation supports at least three metric sources (runtime stats, Datadog, and internal quality eval service)
Auto-rollback triggers, hold, and manual override actions are implemented and audited
E2E test coverage for traffic split calculations, schedule enforcement, and rollback actions
design_decisions: Use a declarative rollout object (stateless controller) stored in the control plane; runtime agents poll/subscribe for ephemeral enforcement state
Guardrails are defined as boolean predicates over metric windows; evaluation outcomes are historicized for post-mortem
Separate 'policy intent' (authoritative config) from 'execution plan' (computed steps with timestamps) so Console can preview and operators can modify without losing intent
Support pluggable metric adapters (Prometheus/Datadog/custom event exporter) - evaluation runs against normalized metric streams
Allow region-scoped splits and model-variant mapping to support multi-region rollout patterns
tradeoffs: Runtime polling every 5s increases control-plane load vs. event-driven complexity for enforcement; chosen approach: 5s polling with long-poll fallback for high-frequency paths
Keeping policy logic in the control plane simplifies audits but increases window for transient drifts between plan and enforcement; mitigations: short heartbeat and state reconciliation
Early autoscale of enforcement agents reduces rollback latency but increases infra cost—will gate aggressive autoscaling behind Dedicated customers and enterprise tiers
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define JSON/YAML rollout schema and serializer; implement read/write/update APIs in control plane
Phase 2: Build a simulator service that takes rollout intent + metric backfills and emits an execution plan and risk estimate
Phase 3: Implement guardrail evaluator with metric adapters (Datadog, runtime telemetry) and integrate with control plane
Phase 4: Runtime agent enforcement for traffic split updates, shadow routing toggles, and rollback/hold operations
Phase 5: Console integration - preview, dry-run, audit trail, and manual override flows
Phase 6: E2E tests, chaos tests (latency spikes, partial metric loss), and staged dogfooding
api_schema_example:
# Example rollout intent (v1)
name: payroll-model-rollout
strategy:
  type: progressive
  steps:
    - duration: 15m
      traffic_percent: 5
    - duration: 30m
      traffic_percent: 25
    - duration: 1h
      traffic_percent: 50
    - duration: 2h
      traffic_percent: 100
guardrails:
  - name: frontend-5xx-threshold
    source: runtime_errors
    metric: 5xx_rate
    comparator: gt
    threshold: 0.01
    window: 5m
    action: rollback
  - name: p99-latency-slo
    source: datadog
    metric: p99_latency_ms
    comparator: gt
    threshold: 1200
    window: 10m
    action: hold
metrics_collectors:
  - runtime: "https://ingest.internal/runtime-metrics/api"
  - datadog: project:redwood.prod
shadow:
  enabled: true
  percent_of_traffic: 10
notes: "This intent will be simulated before activation. Auto-rollback is enabled for critical guardrails."
test_plan: Unit tests for rollout parser and execution plan generator
Simulator integration tests with synthetic metric traces (latency spike, silent error burst, quiet degradation)
Integration tests: control-plane -> runtime agent -> traffic router end-to-end
Chaos test: drop Datadog feed and verify fail-open/hold behavior per policy
Manual QA: Console preview UX and audit entry validation
rollout_simulation_notes: Simulator uses weighted-mixing assumptions for request distributions and models a realistic KV cache hit rate impact on latency
Risk score composed from weighted metrics: error-rate(40%), latency(30%), quality-delta(20%), cost-delta(10%)
Simulator can run in two modes: optimistic (no external perturbation) and adversarial (injects metric shocks based on historic incident patterns)
comments: 2025-11-20: Initial spec reviewed by SRE (A. Chen). Recommended adding 'hold' action separate from 'rollback' to allow manual review window.
2025-12-08: Product review - agreed to support A/B experiments via 'cohorts' field in schema; deferred cohort UI to Cycle 43.
2026-01-15: Security signoff: encryption of rollout objects at rest required; added KMS key field to schema.
2026-02-28: Integration spike completed for Datadog adapter (PR linked); simulator found a case where p95 is more predictive than p99 for certain models—added to open question list.
2026-03-12: Implementer note: runtime agent now applies split changes via atomic config update to avoid transient inconsistent routing (see runtime PR).
